services.name: GitHub Actions Pipeline Hardening
services.problem: The 2025-26 CI supply-chain attacks (tj-actions, Trivy, Checkmarx actions) stole secrets from pipelines that used version tags and long-lived cloud keys.
deliverables: Audit report with a score per workflow
Every action pinned to a commit SHA
AWS access via OIDC instead of stored keys
Secret scanning, safe pull_request_target, Dependabot with cooldown
Add-on: secrets in git history + "were we affected?" check for the 2025-26 incidents, with a rotation plan
services.access: Works through one pull request - no production access needed.

case_study.title: Locking down CI pipelines after the 2025-26 supply-chain attacks
case_study.summary: Every workflow is scored and explained, then fixed in reviewable pull requests: actions pinned to commit SHAs, least-privilege tokens, injection-safe scripts, and AWS access through OIDC instead of stored keys.
case_study.situation: A team with 5-50 GitHub Actions workflows written over the years by different people, using version tags, default write tokens and an AWS access key stored as a secret.
problem: Attacks such as the tj-actions/changed-files and trivy-action tag hijacks stole secrets from every pipeline that used a moving tag.
Default tokens can write to the repository, and pull_request_target workflows can run untrusted code next to secrets.
A long-lived cloud key in a secret turns a CI compromise into a cloud compromise.
solution: An audit that scores each workflow 0-100 against 16 rules and explains every finding in plain words.
Pull request 1: SHA pins, permissions blocks, safe handling of untrusted input, timeouts, no persisted credentials.
Pull request 2: stored AWS keys replaced by an OIDC role that only main, or a protected environment, can assume.
CI gates (zizmor, actionlint, a pin check) and Dependabot with a cooldown, so it stays fixed.

Optional add-on: a full-history secrets scan on a fresh clone (values never shown or tested) and an incident-exposure check against the tj-actions, reviewdog, Trivy and Checkmarx windows, turned into a rotation plan.
flow: Read-only audit: a score per workflow
PR 2: OIDC role, no stored keys

plan.what: I audit every workflow and read each one by hand to understand its intent (why a self-hosted runner, why pull_request_target).
Pull request 1, one commit per topic so you can review it step by step.
Pull request 2 for OIDC (Terraform module or console steps you apply), the CI gates, and the before/after report.

evidence: Five realistic example workflows score 0/100 (F) before and 100/100 (A) after hardening.
The kit audits itself in CI and fails below 90; findings appear in GitHub's Security tab as SARIF.
The AWS login demo uses a role with zero permissions: it proves 'no stored keys' without any risk.
`ghaudit exposure` checks today's workflows, the git history inside each incident window and the workflow runs in those windows; the kit runs it on itself in CI.
keep: OIDC role as Terraform or console steps
not_included: Rewriting your build or test logic
Using any credential found - every secret is reported by type and location, and its owner rotates it

case_study.title: Finding the waste in a cloud bill, without touching production
case_study.summary: A read-only scan of every region finds idle and outdated resources, prices each one, and turns them into a ranked list of fixes with the exact command. The safe ones are applied together, on a call, after your approval.
case_study.situation: A startup or agency spending $500-5,000 a month on AWS, with nobody whose job is cost. The bill grew with every project, and nobody is sure which resources are still needed.
problem: Resources outlive the projects that created them: unattached disks, load balancers with no targets, idle NAT gateways, instances stopped for months but still paying for storage.
Defaults cost money: gp2 disks, logs kept forever, previous-generation instance types.
Nobody has time to check every region by hand, and fear of breaking something stops the clean-up.
solution: A read-only IAM role that you create and can revoke at any time. The tool cannot change anything.
12 waste checks across every enabled region, each with a monthly saving estimate and a risk level.
A ranked report with the exact command for every fix. Commands that delete something take a snapshot or image first and wait for it.
Budgets and anomaly alerts, so the bill can't drift back unnoticed.

plan.what: You create the read-only role from a template (CloudFormation or Terraform). I run the scan across every region.
I check each finding against Cost Explorer and your context, remove false alarms, and write the report.
Walkthrough call. We apply 3-5 low-risk fixes together; you approve every command.
Budgets and anomaly alerts, a short handover note, and you revoke my access.
A second scan to confirm the savings held and nothing new crept in.

evidence: On a synthetic demo account (simulated with moto), the scan finds 20 issues worth $616.37 a month: 4 high, 7 medium, 5 low and 4 informational.
Every finding carries the exact AWS CLI command, and the sample report prints cleanly to PDF.
46 automated tests, including one that records every API call of a full scan and proves the client's read-only policy covers it.
keep: HTML and PDF report ranked by monthly saving
not_included: Re-architecting applications or buying Savings Plans for you (advice only)
Any change without your explicit approval

Scored report with the top 5 risks in plain English
Every fix as code: Terraform module inputs or one command
India: DPDP technical-safeguards view and 72-hour breach runbook
services.access: Read-only role (SecurityAudit + ViewOnlyAccess) that can never read your data; you delete it at the end.

case_study.title: Closing the basic gaps behind most cloud breaches - with fixes as code and a retest
case_study.summary: A read-only check of 25 AWS settings, built on the open-source Prowler scanner and reviewed by hand, ranks what matters for your company, delivers every fix as Terraform or a single command, and proves it with a retest.
case_study.situation: A startup or agency with one to three AWS accounts set up quickly over the years by different people, now facing a customer security questionnaire, a first enterprise deal, or India's DPDP Rules.
problem: Public buckets, SSH open to the internet and secrets in Lambda variables are found by automated scanners within hours.
Nobody switched on CloudTrail, GuardDuty or spend alerts, so a stolen key would be noticed on the monthly bill.
Generic scanners print hundreds of findings with no priorities, and nobody has time to turn them into fixes.
solution: A read-only role with an external ID and an explicit deny on reading data; your own CloudTrail records every call.
Prowler runs 48 curated checks; two native checks add spend alerts and CI/CD keys; every finding is reviewed by a person.
A scored report (A-F) with the top five risks in plain English and the evidence for each control.
Fixes as code: inputs of an open-source Terraform security-baseline module, or one reviewed command. You apply them; I never need write access.
A retest scan shows the new score, what was fixed and what is still open.

plan.what: We sign a short authorisation letter naming the account, regions and dates; you create the read-only role from my CloudFormation template.
I run the scan and review every finding by hand: false positives out, intended exceptions noted, risks ranked for your business.
Report, fix pack and a 45-minute walkthrough. You apply the fixes, with my help on a screen share if you like.
Retest scan and updated report; you delete the role and I confirm the scan files are deleted.

evidence: On a simulated account seeded with a fictional company's typical mistakes, the baseline scores 31/100 (F) before and 97/100 (A) after the fix pack - both reports are on this site.
The demo runs the real Prowler checks against a simulated AWS account, and a Terraform sandbox builds a real, deliberately misconfigured account that is scanned and destroyed in one command.
The fix pack is a tested Terraform module with one input per control; my own AWS account runs the same module.
keep: Scored report (HTML and PDF) and findings.csv
Terraform fix pack and one-off commands
For India: DPDP view and a 72-hour breach runbook template
not_included: Penetration testing, incident response or malware removal (I refer you to specialists)
Compliance certification or legal advice - the DPDP view is technical readiness only
Changes made by me in your account

GitHub Actions: tests, lint, image build, vulnerability scan, SBOM and a keyless cosign signature.
Terraform for ECS Fargate (or EC2), the load balancer, the database and alarms, with AWS access through OIDC.
Rolling deployments with health checks and the ECS circuit breaker, plus a one-command rollback.

Hard daily and monthly caps checked before each call, with a safe fallback when anything fails.

services.name: Backup & Restore Drill
services.problem: Most teams have backups but have never restored one - and scripts or AI agents can delete production and its backups with the same credentials.
deliverables: Timed restore into an isolated sandbox
services.access: A scoped role; the drill never touches production data.

case_study.title: Proving the backups restore, and measuring how long it takes
case_study.summary: A backup is restored into an isolated sandbox, the data is proven identical with 13 checks, recovery time and data loss are measured against your targets, and the backups are checked for whether one identity could delete them along with production.
case_study.situation: A SaaS team on RDS or PostgreSQL with automated backups switched on, but nobody has ever restored one, and the recovery time promised in contracts is a guess.
problem: Backups that have never been restored are a hope, not a plan: jobs stop silently, tables go missing, restores take hours.
RTO and RPO are guesses, even when customers or auditors ask for them.
The same credentials can often delete the database and every backup, as an AI agent did to a company's production data in April 2026.
solution: A backup inventory and isolation report: retention, deletion protection, public or shared snapshots, cross-region and cross-account copies, locked vaults, and what your app's role could delete.
A timed restore into a new sandbox instance (snapshot and point in time), never over production.
13 data checks against a manifest: row counts, checksums, broken relationships, business totals.
A report with RTO and RPO against your targets, and a runbook your team can follow.

plan.what: Agree targets and checks; you create a scoped role; isolation report.
First drill from the latest snapshot, verified inside your network, sandbox deleted the same day.
Point-in-time drill and comparison with your targets.
Report, runbook and walkthrough.

evidence: Every push to the kit's repository runs a real restore of 5,000 synthetic customers and all 13 checks.
On AWS, the kit restores RDS from a snapshot or a point in time into a sandbox with its own security group, then deletes it.
Isolation checks flag public snapshots, shared-but-not-copied snapshots, missing cross-region copies and app roles that could delete backups.
keep: Two timed drills (snapshot and point in time)
not_included: Changes to production settings (quoted as drill + hardening)

deliverables: Before/after security score (Lynis) with every finding explained
Key-only SSH, firewall, fail2ban and nightly security patches
HTTPS with security headers, backups with a tested restore
Everything as Ansible code in your repository: rebuild any server in minutes
Optional: releases with health checks and one-command rollback

services.access: A key-only user with sudo, on a snapshot or staging copy first - never a root password.

case_study.title: Hardening a hand-built server, and making it rebuildable
case_study.summary: The server is audited (a before score), hardened with Ansible in one idempotent run, given HTTPS, backups and monitoring, audited again (an after score), and checked for drift every night. Everything is code, so it can be rebuilt in minutes.
case_study.situation: A small company running its site or app on a VPS or EC2 instance set up by hand years ago: password SSH, no firewall, months of missing patches, no tested backups, and nobody who could rebuild it.
problem: Password SSH and open ports are scanned by bots within minutes of a server going online.
Missing patches and no backups turn one bad day into a lost business.
If the server dies, nobody knows how it was built.
solution: A snapshot first, then a read-only Lynis audit: the 'before' score with every finding explained.
Ansible roles for key-only SSH (validated before reload, so you can't be locked out), a default-deny firewall, fail2ban and nightly security patches.
HTTPS with security headers, the app in a systemd sandbox, backups with a tested restore, and monitoring.
An 'after' audit, a nightly drift check, and releases with a health gate and automatic rollback.
Optional add-on: email and domain security from public DNS only - one SPF record, DKIM for every sender, DMARC moved from monitoring to reject over a few weeks so no real mail is lost, and CAA.

plan.what: Snapshot (by you), key-only access for me, the 'before' audit; we agree what may change.
Hardening on a staging copy first, then the live server; HTTPS, backups and a restore test.
The 'after' audit, the report, and handover of the Ansible code into your repository.

evidence: In ServerForge's container lab, the Lynis score goes from 60 to 80 after one Ansible run (real servers score differently; the report shows both runs).
CI runs every role twice and fails if the second run changes anything.
Releases go out one server at a time behind a health gate with automatic rollback; a nightly check-mode run catches hand edits.
not_included: Managing the server month to month (care plan available)
